prerequisites: Starting build 067c1646 installed with the installation guide's files (TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1,::1 as its .env.example suggested) and populated with its scripts/seed (light, random seed 7, e-signature on the seed's stand-in): 22 users, 36 Contracts, 18 Matters, 30 Entities, 106 Documents with 127 Versions and 174 stored files, 3 Envelopes (2 signed, 1 declined).

Added on the starting build: a relay with an SMTP password, an AI connector key (stand-in), an SSO provider with a client secret (OIDC discovery stand-in), MCP on with Team and Administration in the ceiling and an Administrator's API key naming them, and Maximum file size 40 MiB saved in Settings → Advanced.
Target 4ca41822 selected by the guide; pre-upgrade coherent backup retained.
scenarios.expected: Accounts, permissions, records, files and required encrypted configuration survive the supported upgrade; recovery is a restore of the pre-upgrade backup into a separate target, not a downgrade.
scenarios.actual: Before you start: revision, images, project, COMPOSE_FILE, local storage and the Saved in OpenLaw field (Maximum file size 40) recorded; baseline journal 172 rows ending 0171_m41-oauth-clients, 112 tables, per-table row digests, 174 file hashes, digests of the 8 sealed columns. Prepare step 1: git status (only untracked operator files), git fetch origin, rev-parse. Step 2: git checkout --detach 4ca41822 exit 128 (unpublished pin, see limitations), then after a local fetch: checkout, OPENLAW_BUILD_COMMIT, config --quiet and build (17 s) left all 4 containers unchanged; app and worker resolve to the same image; postgres:16. Step 3: compose.yml diff empty; the guide's gateway read gave 10.245.72.1 and TRUSTED_PROXIES moved from 127.0.0.1,::1 to it. Outstanding work: pg-boss completed only; Envelopes declined 1, signed 2. Step 4: backup steps 1 to 4 with app and worker stopped; 884 TOC entries, 174 files, SHA256SUMS verified in the retained copy. Start step 1: up, ps, port 127.0.0.1:24720, readiness in 4 s, journal 184 rows ending 0183_sso-provider-name (12 added in one start), app and worker 0 restarts and running, no error lines. After the upgrade and before new work: all 174 file hashes and all 8 sealed-column digests unchanged; 102 of 113 tables have identical row digests; count changes contract_statuses 10→11, document_types 6→7, envelope_launches new, runtime_status and sessions (heartbeat and sign-ins); same-count differences only in org_settings (ceiling), contract_envelopes and sso_providers (new columns), users, api_keys and notifications (activity). Step 2 in the browser: the Administrator signed in through the origin and the guide's remoteAddress command showed only the browser's 192.168.122.1 for the sign-in; a Legal Team Member got 404 and 'Contract not found' on Confidential C-4 (404 before too) while C-1 opened; a Business User signed in with a fresh magic link and got 403 (staff API) and 404 (Portal API) on C-4. Step 3: C-1 to C-3, M-1 and an Entity open with their Field values; Settings → Contracts → Statuses shows the 10 earlier names plus Partially signed last in the Signature Stage; Settings → Documents → Contracts shows the 6 earlier types plus Partially signed just before Executed, order kept; 8 representative original, later and executed Version hashes match. Step 4: a new upload was processed; Send test email through the relay saved on the starting build arrived; AI Test connection said 'Connection successful.' (the stand-in accepts only the saved key); System status Refresh showed API and Worker Running and Current; Maximum file size still 40, Saved in OpenLaw. Listed changes: the ceiling lost team and administration while the key still records them, so the key lists no Team or Administration Tool; after the Administrator selected them again it listed openlaw_audit_log_query and openlaw_settings_get; the SSO provider has an empty name and Settings → Authentication lists it as doc032-idp with Remove doc032-idp; all 3 Envelopes have completes_contract=true and no Version is Partially signed. Step 5: jobs completed, none failed; worker running; an old tab navigated without the reload notice. Negative: the retained pre-upgrade backup restored into the empty openlaw-doc032-oprecover on the starting build 067c1646 with the retained keys: journal 172 rows, 174 file hashes and all sealed digests match, the post-backup upload is absent, the Legal Team Member stays refused on C-4, and a test email went through the restored relay. The migrated database was never opened by an older image.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by an agent that did not write or source-review the guide; container-operation by an agent acting as a fictional operator, with browser checks as an Administrator, a Legal Team Member and a Business User; not a human operator study.

Publication precondition: 4ca41822 is on no GitHub branch. After the guide's git clone from GitHub, git checkout --detach 4ca41822 exits 128 with 'fatal: unable to read tree' (install Prepare step 1; upgrade Prepare step 2 after git fetch origin). The walkthrough fetched the pin from the local repository into the GitHub clone and continued; the guide text is correct once the revision is published on a branch or tag. Publish it before this edition is released.

Fixture deviations on the starting build (not guide steps): the 067c1646 seed stops at random seed 7 with 409 'This person is already on the team.' (fixed later in 00528360), so that one-file fix was applied to a scratch copy; its signing stand-in reports a loopback base_uri that a containerised app cannot reach, so the copy answered as its network alias; the seed ran with the lab overlay's settings (SETUP_TOKEN, AUTH_RATE_LIMIT=off, SIGNING_STANDIN, DOCUSIGN_BASE_URL, SMTP_URL, SMTP_FROM), all removed and the containers recreated before the baseline.

The starting build has no Team or Administration Tools, so the Toolset change was observed through the ceiling and the target's Tools, not through a Tool the key used before the upgrade. No organization had its own partially_signed Status or type, so the author's edge case was not exercised.

Host deviation: compose.doc032-net.yml in COMPOSE_FILE gives explicit subnets because this host's Docker default address pools are exhausted. The same-host proxy was Caddy on the host network bound to a local-only address with an internal CA. Builds used a warm cache.
Mail went to an owned Mailpit relay; the AI provider, the identity provider and the signing provider were owned stand-ins. None is a live provider.
An old browser tab did not show 'This part of OpenLaw was updated. Reload to continue.'; the guide says it can.
Every project, support container, network, volume and private backup was removed after the walk.
